jurisdiction.publisher: City of Cape Town (Corporate GIS / Open Data Team), metropolitan municipality, South Africa; portal hosted on Esri ArcGIS Hub

measurements.catalog_census_2026_10_29: 265 datasets in the DCAT-US feed. Task-shaped highlights: Service Requests Jan 2023 to Present (4.5M rows, live daily - carried to za-cct-c3-service-request-surge, ready); Suburb Level Water Billing 2021 to September 2026 (219,184 rows, 787 suburbs x 69 months x 6 billing classes); Suburb Level Electricity Billing (102,809 rows, same shape); Prepaid Electricity by Suburbs and Tariffs Jan 2024 to Sep 2026; Municipal Arrears Suburbs and Service Type 2025 to Sep 2026 (historic items back to 2018); Dam Levels from 2000 / Jan 2012 to April 2026 (stale ~5-6 months on the Hub vs the City's live daily dam-levels page); Rainfall Jan 2000 until April 2026 (stale ~6 months on the Hub); Traffic Accidents (Crash Data) Statistics 2019 to 2024; Fire Incidence 2009 to 2016 + Jan 2017 to July 2022 (ended); Electricity Voltage dips up to Sep 2026; Library circulation/membership monthly to Sep-Oct 2026; Air Quality NO2/O3/PM10/SO2 2022 to 2024; Emergency response times; Inland Water Quality Results (Raw).
measurements.billing_mask_veto_2026_10_29: DECISIVE for the suburb-level water/electricity billing panel: the entire billing family is ~98-100% '*' masked for every month before April 2026 and fully unmasked only from 2026-04 onward (measured on water Domestic: 44,713/49,947 rows masked across 63 months 2020-12..2026-02, 0% masked 2026-04..2026-09, 2026-03 absent; electricity Domestic: 100% masked 2020-12..2026-02, 0% 2026-04..09; water non-Domestic classes 92.7-100% masked in 2023-06 vs 0% in 2026-09). The unmask regime change coincides with the item republish dates (April 2026). Quantity semantics resolved before the veto: litres (Amount/Quantity = 0.044 ZAR/L ~= R44/kl, the CCT tariff band; Quantity/record ~2,775 L). Split capacity for a billing-direction task is therefore nil today.
measurements.portal_hygiene_observations: The publisher freezes deprecated datasets with in-page deprecation notices pointing at successors (Service Requests item deprecated 2026-10-06); per-year historic items are linked from live items (C3 back to 2011); the Hub footer carries boilerplate 'Copyright ... All rights reserved.' while per-dataset licence fields point at the Open Data terms; old ASPX portal (web1.capetown.gov.za) 302s to an error page.
measurements.unprobed_leftovers: Emergency response times, Electricity Voltage dips, Library statistics, Inland Water Quality (Raw), Prepaid Electricity and Municipal Arrears (mask regime unmeasured) - none carried to formulation this session.

rejection_reason: PARK (coverage, not a rejection of the data): the portal's licence posture is workable (class A, quoted instruments) and it hosts real unit-grain series, but the most task-shaped family (suburb-level water/electricity billing) is decisively masked before 2026-04, leaving ~6 unmasked months - no split capacity; one live unit-grain task (C3 service requests) was carried to its own ready record this session; remaining datasets are either stale on the Hub (dam levels, rainfall: ~5-6 months behind the City's live pages), ended (fire incidence July 2022), or unprobed.
review: Coverage record preserving a full portal census and the billing-mask veto so a future tick does not re-derive it. The billing task becomes viable only after the unmasked regime accumulates ~18+ months (>= ~Q3 2027), or if the publisher backfills history unmasked.
next_action: Reopen the suburb-level billing task ONLY when the unmasked window (since 2026-04) covers roughly 18+ months, i.e. check again from ~2027-10, or earlier on evidence the publisher backfilled pre-2026-04 history unmasked. Re-census the DCAT feed only when a new task-shaped unit-grain series appears (Emergency response times, Voltage dips, Library stats and Water Quality remain the unprobed candidates; probe them in a later Africa tick before opening new portals). za-cct-c3-service-request-surge (ready) is this portal's contribution to the queue.
